observations.caveat: House and Senate bill shares use enacted bills from each originating chamber divided by that chamber's introduced bills. Joint resolutions are excluded from those shares. The 274 laws include five House joint resolutions; dividing 274 by only House bills would mix origins and measure types. Vetoed measures include joint resolutions.

Law total includes bills introduced in 2023 and carried into 2024. Do not divide 111 by the 605 bills introduced only in 2024. Bill vetoes and line-item vetoes have different denominators. Special session is excluded.

Appendix A's bill action summary gives 583 introduced, 72 passed, 69 enacted, and 3 vetoed. Its adjacent table separately labels five partial vetoes in an enacted category that does not reconcile arithmetically with the 72 passed bills; use the bill action summary for these figures and do not add five to 69. No override count is established here.

The city's session-statistics counts are activity totals, not necessarily a same-cohort introduction-to-enactment rate. Enacted is different from codified; resolutions and other actions are separate. This large city's count is not a typical U.S. city rate.

Counted the county's numbered entries 2024-001 through 2024-045 with 033 absent. The page is an ordinance list; it does not establish introduced-versus-adopted statuses or a general county-size rate. Many entries amend appropriations or staffing.

coverageGaps.allStateSessionSeriesReason: NCSL's broad Bill Information Service, including session statistics, requires member access. Public topic databases cannot be combined into an all-subject 50-state total without duplicate and scope controls. This packet contains only official Kansas and New Mexico all-bill snapshots.
coverageGaps.repealReason: Amendment, explicit repeal, sunset, and supersession are distinct outcomes. The located academic repeal study follows landmark federal enactments, not the population of all federal and state laws; it cannot support a general rate or time-to-repeal constant.
coverageGaps.localVolumeBySizeReason: The three local observations are individual jurisdictions with different ordinance definitions and no matched population-size sampling. They demonstrate nonzero local lawmaking, not a size-stratified annual distribution.

gameplayCalibration.reason: Preserve jurisdiction-specific session length, carryover, bill cohort, chamber origin, veto outcome, and local ordinance definition before deriving game probabilities. Do not apply one state, congressional, or city sample to all places.
